subject: math
title: Cartesian Coordinates and Graphing: Four Quadrants, Shapes and Tables of Values
seo_title: Grade 7 Cartesian Coordinates and Graphing Worksheets: Free Math with Answer Key (BC Curriculum)
meta_desc: Free Grade 7 math worksheets on Cartesian coordinates for the BC curriculum: name the four quadrants, read and plot points, find missing vertices and side lengths of shapes on the grid, and graph tables of values in BC word problems. 100 questions with an answer key, good FSA numeracy practice.
key_big: In (x, y), x tells you left or right and y tells you up or down. A minus sign means left or down.
key_sub: Quadrants I to IV go counterclockwise from the top right. A point on an axis is in no quadrant. A side along a grid line is larger minus smaller, so from −3 to 4 is 4 − (−3) = 7. Each column of a table of values is one point to plot.
body_html:
The four quadrants

The Cartesian plane has two number lines. The x-axis goes across and the y-axis goes up and down. They cross at the origin, (0, 0), and cut the plane into four quadrants. The quadrants are numbered I, II, III, IV counterclockwise, starting at the top right.

An ordered pair (x, y) always gives x first. The sign tells the direction. Positive x: right. Negative x: left. Positive y: up. Negative y: down.

QuadrantWhereSigns (x, y)Example
Itop right(+, +)(4, 2)
IItop left(−, +)(−3, 4)
IIIbottom left(−, −)(−5, −1)
IVbottom right(+, −)(2, −6)

A point on an axis, like (0, 5) or (−6, 0), is not in any quadrant.

Example

Which quadrant is (5, −4) in?

x is positive (right) and y is negative (down). Right and down is the bottom right.

Answer: Quadrant IV

Shapes on the plane

When a side runs along a grid line, only one coordinate changes. Its length is the larger value minus the smaller one. If the side crosses an axis, subtracting a negative number adds: 4 − (−3) = 7.

Example

Find the perimeter and the area of rectangle ABCD above.

Length 7 units, width 5 units. Perimeter = 7 + 5 + 7 + 5 = 24 units. Area = 7 × 5 = 35 square units.

Answer: 24 units and 35 square units

Missing vertex

A rectangle has vertices (−3, 3), (4, 3) and (4, −2). Find the fourth vertex.

The fourth vertex lines up with (−3, 3) and with (4, −2). Take x = −3 from the first and y = −2 from the second.

Answer: (−3, −2)

Graph a table of values

Each column of a table of values is one ordered pair (x, y). Plot every pair. If y changes by the same amount each time x goes up by 1, the points lie on a straight line.

x01234
y−4−2024
Example

A diver starts at the surface and goes down 2 m each minute. Write the point for 3 minutes.

x = 3 minutes. Below the surface is negative: y = −2 × 3 = −6.

Answer: (3, −6), in Quadrant IV

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
Swapping the numbers: plotting (−3, 4) at (4, −3)Move across first (x), then up or down (y)
Dropping the minus signNegative x means left; negative y means down
Numbering the quadrants clockwiseGo counterclockwise: I top right, II top left, III bottom left, IV bottom right
Saying (0, 5) is in Quadrant IA point on an axis is not in any quadrant
From −3 to 4 doing 4 − 3 = 1Subtract the negative: 4 − (−3) = 7
Counting grid lines instead of spacesCount the jumps between lines; the starting line is 0
Reading a table across the wrong rowEach column is one pair: top number x, bottom number y

faq.q: What do Grade 7 students learn about Cartesian coordinates in BC?
faq.a: The BC Grade 7 math curriculum includes Cartesian coordinates and graphing. Students plot and read points in all four quadrants, work with shapes on the grid and graph ordered pairs, for example from a table of values.

faq.q: How are the four quadrants numbered?
faq.a: Counterclockwise from the top right: Quadrant I (+, +), II (−, +), III (−, −) and IV (+, −). A point on an axis, like (0, 5), is not in any quadrant.

faq.q: How do you find the length of a side on a coordinate grid?
faq.a: If the side runs along a grid line, subtract the coordinates that change: larger minus smaller. From (−3, 2) to (4, 2), the length is 4 − (−3) = 7 units.

faq.q: Are coordinates on the Grade 7 FSA?
faq.a: The Grade 7 FSA numeracy questions draw on the math students learn in BC, so reading and plotting points and graphing tables of values is useful practice. These worksheets come with an answer key.

sets.title: The four quadrants and the axes

items.q: Which quadrant is the point (4, 2) in?
items.e: x is positive (right) and y is positive (up), so (4, 2) is in Quadrant I. The quadrants go counterclockwise from the top right: I, II, III, IV.

items.q: Which quadrant is the point (−3, 5) in?
items.e: x is negative (left) and y is positive (up), so (−3, 5) is in Quadrant II. The quadrants go counterclockwise from the top right: I, II, III, IV.

items.q: Which quadrant is the point (−1, −6) in?
items.e: x is negative (left) and y is negative (down), so (−1, −6) is in Quadrant III. The quadrants go counterclockwise from the top right: I, II, III, IV.

items.q: Which quadrant is the point (5, −4) in?
items.e: x is positive (right) and y is negative (down), so (5, −4) is in Quadrant IV. The quadrants go counterclockwise from the top right: I, II, III, IV.

items.q: Which quadrant is the point (−6, 3) in?
items.e: x is negative (left) and y is positive (up), so (−6, 3) is in Quadrant II. The quadrants go counterclockwise from the top right: I, II, III, IV.

items.q: Which quadrant is the point (2, −1) in?
items.e: x is positive (right) and y is negative (down), so (2, −1) is in Quadrant IV. The quadrants go counterclockwise from the top right: I, II, III, IV.

items.q: Which quadrant is the point (6, 6) in?
items.e: x is positive (right) and y is positive (up), so (6, 6) is in Quadrant I. The quadrants go counterclockwise from the top right: I, II, III, IV.

items.q: Which quadrant is the point (−4, −2) in?
items.e: x is negative (left) and y is negative (down), so (−4, −2) is in Quadrant III. The quadrants go counterclockwise from the top right: I, II, III, IV.

items.q: Where is the point (0, 5)?
items.e: x = 0, so the point does not move left or right. It goes up 5 along the y-axis. A point on an axis is not in any quadrant.

items.q: Where is the point (3, 0)?
items.e: y = 0, so the point does not move up or down. It goes right 3 along the x-axis. It is not in any quadrant.

items.q: What is the name of the point (0, 0), where the axes cross?
items.e: The x-axis and the y-axis cross at (0, 0). This point is called the origin. Every point is plotted by starting there.

items.q: In which quadrant is the x-coordinate negative and the y-coordinate positive?
items.e: Negative x means left and positive y means up. Left and up is the top-left part: Quadrant II.

items.q: In which quadrant are both coordinates negative?
items.e: Negative x means left and negative y means down. Left and down is the bottom-left part: Quadrant III.

items.q: What are the signs of the coordinates of a point in Quadrant IV?
items.e: Quadrant IV is the bottom-right part. Right means x is positive and down means y is negative: (+, −).

items.q: Which point is in Quadrant III?
items.e: Quadrant III is the bottom-left part: x negative (left) and y negative (down). (−2, −5) is left 2 and down 5.

items.q: A point is on the x-axis. What must be true?
items.e: On the x-axis, you do not move up or down from the origin, so y = 0. Examples: (−5, 0) and (4, 0).

items.q: Which point is in Quadrant III?
items.e: Point D is at (−4, −3). x is negative (left) and y is negative (down), so (−4, −3) is in Quadrant III. The quadrants go counterclockwise from the top right: I, II, III, IV.

items.q: Which point is in Quadrant IV?
items.e: Point C is at (5, −2). x is positive (right) and y is negative (down), so (5, −2) is in Quadrant IV. The quadrants go counterclockwise from the top right: I, II, III, IV. Point A is in Quadrant II: numbering the quadrants clockwise would wrongly call it IV.

items.q: Mei says (4, −1) is in Quadrant II. What mistake did she make?
items.e: (4, −1) is right and down: Quadrant IV. The quadrants go counterclockwise: I top right, II top left, III bottom left, IV bottom right.

items.q: Leah says (−6, 0) is in Quadrant III because it has a minus sign. Is she right?
c: No, it is in Quadrant II
No, it is on the y-axis
No, it is on the x-axis, not in a quadrant
items.e: y = 0, so the point sits on the x-axis, 6 units left of the origin. Points on an axis are not in any quadrant.

items.q: What are the coordinates of point A?
items.e: Start at the origin, go right 3, then up 5. Point A is at (3, 5). Write the x-coordinate first; a minus sign means left or down.

items.q: What are the coordinates of point B?
items.e: Start at the origin, go left 4, then up 2. Point B is at (−4, 2). Write the x-coordinate first; a minus sign means left or down.

items.q: What are the coordinates of point C?
items.e: Start at the origin, go left 2, then down 6. Point C is at (−2, −6). Write the x-coordinate first; a minus sign means left or down. (−6, −2) is point D: the numbers are swapped.

items.q: What are the coordinates of point E?
items.e: Start at the origin, go right 5, then down 3. Point E is at (5, −3). Write the x-coordinate first; a minus sign means left or down.

items.q: What are the coordinates of point F?
items.e: Start at the origin, go left 5, then up 4. Point F is at (−5, 4). Write the x-coordinate first; a minus sign means left or down. (4, −5) is point G: the numbers are swapped.

items.q: What are the coordinates of point H?
items.e: Start at the origin, go right 6, then down 1. Point H is at (6, −1). Write the x-coordinate first; a minus sign means left or down.

items.q: What are the coordinates of point J?
items.e: Start at the origin, go left 3, then down 3. Point J is at (−3, −3). Write the x-coordinate first; a minus sign means left or down.

items.q: What are the coordinates of point K?
items.e: Start at the origin, go 0 left or right, then up 4. Point K is at (0, 4). Write the x-coordinate first; a minus sign means left or down. (4, 0) is point L: the numbers are swapped.

items.q: What are the coordinates of point M?
items.e: Start at the origin, go left 1, then up 6. Point M is at (−1, 6). Write the x-coordinate first; a minus sign means left or down.

items.q: What are the coordinates of point N?
items.e: Start at the origin, go left 6, then 0 up or down. Point N is at (−6, 0). Write the x-coordinate first; a minus sign means left or down.

items.q: What are the coordinates of point T?
items.e: Start at the origin, go right 1, then down 5. Point T is at (1, −5). Write the x-coordinate first; a minus sign means left or down. (−5, 1) is point U: the numbers are swapped.

items.q: What are the coordinates of point V?
items.e: Start at the origin, go 0 left or right, then down 3. Point V is at (0, −3). Write the x-coordinate first; a minus sign means left or down.

items.q: What is the x-coordinate of point R?
items.e: Point R is 5 units to the left of the y-axis, so x = −5. Left means negative. (3 is its y-coordinate.)

items.q: What is the y-coordinate of point S?
items.e: Point S is 4 units below the x-axis, so y = −4. Down means negative. (2 is its x-coordinate.)

items.q: Which point has an x-coordinate of −3?
items.e: x = −3 means 3 units left of the y-axis. Only point B is there, at (−3, 4). Point A has y = −3, not x.

items.q: Which point has a y-coordinate of −2?
items.e: y = −2 means 2 units below the x-axis. Only point D is there, at (5, −2). Point A has x = −2, not y.

items.q: Which point has two negative coordinates?
items.e: Both coordinates are negative when the point is left of the y-axis and below the x-axis (Quadrant III). Point A is at (−2, −5).

items.q: Which two points have the same y-coordinate?
items.e: P is at (−4, 1) and Q is at (3, 1). Both are 1 unit above the x-axis, so both have y = 1. Q and T have the same x-coordinate, 3, not the same y-coordinate.

items.q: Ji-woo writes the coordinates of point W as (5, −2). What mistake did she make?
c: She counted the grid lines, not the spaces
items.e: W is left 2 and up 5, so it is at (−2, 5). Ji-woo put the numbers in the wrong order. Always write x (across) first, then y (up or down).

items.q: A point is 6 units to the left of the y-axis and 4 units below the x-axis. What are its coordinates?
items.e: Left of the y-axis means x is negative: x = −6. Below the x-axis means y is negative: y = −4. The point is (−6, −4).

sets.title: Plot points in all four quadrants

items.q: Which point is at (2, 5)?
items.e: Start at the origin, go right 2, then up 5: that is point C. Point A is at (5, 2): the numbers are swapped.

items.q: Which point is at (−4, 3)?
items.e: Start at the origin, go left 4, then up 3: that is point B. Point A is at (3, −4): the numbers are swapped.

items.q: Which point is at (−5, −2)?
items.e: Start at the origin, go left 5, then down 2: that is point A. Point B is at (−2, −5): the numbers are swapped.

items.q: Which point is at (3, −6)?
items.e: Start at the origin, go right 3, then down 6: that is point D. Point A is at (−6, 3): the numbers are swapped.

items.q: Which point is at (−2, 6)?
items.e: Start at the origin, go left 2, then up 6: that is point C. Point A is at (6, −2): the numbers are swapped.

items.q: Which point is at (6, −4)?
items.e: Start at the origin, go right 6, then down 4: that is point D. Point A is at (−4, 6): the numbers are swapped.

items.q: Which point is at (−6, −5)?
items.e: Start at the origin, go left 6, then down 5: that is point A. Point B is at (−5, −6): the numbers are swapped.

items.q: Which point is at (0, −5)?
items.e: Start at the origin, go 0 left or right, then down 5: that is point B. Point A is at (−5, 0): the numbers are swapped.

items.q: Which point is at (4, 0)?
items.e: Start at the origin, go right 4, then 0 up or down: that is point A. Point B is at (0, 4): the numbers are swapped.

items.q: Which point is at (−2, 4)?
items.e: Start at the origin, go left 2, then up 4: that is point C. Point A is at (4, −2): the numbers are swapped.

items.q: To plot (−3, 6), what do you do first from the origin?
items.e: The first number, −3, is the x-coordinate. It is negative, so go left 3. Then go up 6.

items.q: To plot (4, −2), you go right 4 from the origin. What do you do next?
items.e: The second number, −2, is the y-coordinate. It is negative, so go down 2.

items.q: Sofia was asked to plot (5, −1). She plotted point X. What mistake did she make?
c: She went up or down first
She counted the grid lines, not the spaces
items.e: X is at (−1, 5). To plot (5, −1), go right 5 first (x), then down 1 (y). Sofia used the numbers in the wrong order.

items.q: Mei wants to plot A (2, 3), B (−4, 1), C (−3, −2), D (5, −4). Which point did she plot in the wrong place?
items.e: Point D should be at (5, −4), but it is at (−4, 5): x and y are swapped. The other points are correct.

items.q: You plot (−4, 3) and (5, 3) and join them with a line segment. What kind of segment is it?
items.e: Both points have y = 3, so both are 3 units up. The segment runs straight across, parallel to the x-axis.

items.q: Which point would you plot in the same quadrant as (−2, −6)?
items.e: (−2, −6) is left and down: Quadrant III. (−5, −1) is also left and down.

items.q: Which point would you plot on the y-axis?
items.e: A point on the y-axis does not move left or right, so x = 0. (0, −3) goes down 3 along the y-axis.

items.q: You plot a point 3 units to the right of (−5, 2). Where is the new point?
items.e: Moving right changes only x. −5 + 3 = −2, so the new point is (−2, 2). y stays 2.

items.q: Jasleen plots the point (−3, −4). Which moves from the origin are correct?
items.e: x = −3: go left 3. y = −4: go down 4. Always do x first.

items.q: You plot a point 2 units below (4, 1). Where is the new point?
items.e: Moving down changes only y. 1 − 2 = −1, so the new point is (4, −1). x stays 4.

sets.title: Shapes on the Cartesian plane: missing vertices and side lengths

items.q: A, B and C are three vertices of rectangle ABCD. What are the coordinates of D?
items.e: D lines up with A and with C. It has the same x-coordinate as A (−4) and the same y-coordinate as C (−2). D is (−4, −2).

items.q: A, B and C are three vertices of rectangle ABCD. What are the coordinates of D?
items.e: D lines up with A and with C. It has the same y-coordinate as A (−1) and the same x-coordinate as C (3). D is (3, −1).

items.q: A rectangle has vertices at (−3, −2), (4, −2) and (4, 5). What are the coordinates of the fourth vertex?
items.e: The sides of the rectangle run along grid lines. The fourth vertex is across from (4, −2). It takes x from one neighbour and y from the other: (−3, 5).

items.q: A rectangle has vertices at (1, −6), (−5, −6) and (−5, −1). What are the coordinates of the fourth vertex?
items.e: The sides of the rectangle run along grid lines. The fourth vertex is across from (−5, −6). It takes x from one neighbour and y from the other: (1, −1).

items.q: What is the length of the line segment from (−3, 2) to (4, 2)?
items.e: Only x changes, from −3 to 4. Length = 4 − (−3) = 7 units (larger − smaller). The segment crosses an axis: 3 units on one side and 4 on the other, 3 + 4 = 7.

items.q: What is the length of segment PQ?
items.e: P is at (5, −4) and Q is at (5, 1). Only y changes, from −4 to 1. Length = 1 − (−4) = 5 units (larger − smaller). The segment crosses an axis: 4 units on one side and 1 on the other, 4 + 1 = 5.

items.q: What is the length of the line segment from (−6, −1) to (−2, −1)?
items.e: Only x changes, from −6 to −2. Length = −2 − (−6) = 4 units (larger − smaller). Both ends are on the same side of the axis, so do not add 6 and 2.

items.q: What is the length of the line segment from (−2, −5) to (−2, 3)?
items.e: Only y changes, from −5 to 3. Length = 3 − (−5) = 8 units (larger − smaller). The segment crosses an axis: 5 units on one side and 3 on the other, 5 + 3 = 8.

items.q: How far is the point (−5, 4) from the x-axis?
items.e: The distance to the x-axis is how far up or down the point is: the y-coordinate, 4 units. (5 units is the distance to the y-axis.)

items.q: What is the perimeter of rectangle ABCD?
items.e: Length AB: 2 − (−4) = 6 units. Width BC: 3 − (−1) = 4 units. Perimeter = 6 + 4 + 6 + 4 = 20 units. (24 is the area; 10 adds only two sides.)

items.q: A rectangle has vertices at (−3, 4), (2, 4), (2, −2) and (−3, −2). What is its area?
items.e: Length: 2 − (−3) = 5 units. Width: 4 − (−2) = 6 units. Area = 5 × 6 = 30 square units. (22 is the perimeter; 6 × 7 = 42 comes from counting grid lines.)

items.q: What is the area of triangle ABC?
items.e: Base AB: 3 − (−3) = 6 units. Height BC: 2 − (−2) = 4 units. Area = base × height ÷ 2 = 6 × 4 ÷ 2 = 12 square units. (24 forgets to divide by 2.)

items.q: The points (−3, 1), (2, 1), (2, −4) and (−3, −4) are joined in order. What shape do they make?
c: a rectangle that is not a square
a parallelogram with no right angles
items.e: The sides run along grid lines, so the angles are right angles. Across: 2 − (−3) = 5. Down: 1 − (−4) = 5. All four sides are 5 units, so it is a square.

items.q: Two vertices of a square are (−2, 1) and (2, 1). The other two vertices are above them. Where are they?
items.e: The side length is 2 − (−2) = 4 units. Go up 4 from y = 1: 1 + 4 = 5. The vertices are (−2, 5) and (2, 5). (Using 2 as the side length gives y = 3; counting grid lines gives 5 units and y = 6.)

items.q: Emma says the segment from (−3, 6) to (4, 6) is 1 unit long. What mistake did she make?
c: She counted the grid lines, not the spaces
items.e: The length is 4 − (−3) = 7 units. Subtracting a negative is the same as adding: 4 + 3 = 7.

items.q: The points (−4, −1) and (−4, 5) are joined. Which is true?
c: It is a vertical segment 4 units long
It is a vertical segment 7 units long
It is a horizontal segment 6 units long
It is a vertical segment 6 units long
items.e: Both points have x = −4, so the segment goes straight up and down. Length = 5 − (−1) = 6 units.

items.q: A rectangle has vertices at (−5, 2), (3, 2) and (3, −4). In which quadrant is the fourth vertex?
items.e: The fourth vertex takes x from (−5, 2) and y from (3, −4): (−5, −4). x is negative and y is negative, so it is in Quadrant III.

items.q: Lucas draws a map of Stanley Park on a grid where each unit is 10 m. The playground is at (−3, 4) and the washroom is at (−3, −2). How far apart are they?
items.e: Only y changes: 4 − (−2) = 6 units. Each unit is 10 m, so 6 × 10 = 60 m. (4 − 2 = 2 gives 20 m; 6 m forgets the scale.)

items.q: Arjun plans a rectangular school garden in Burnaby on a grid map where each unit is 1 m. The corners are at (−4, −3), (3, −3), (3, 1) and (−4, 1). How much fencing goes around the garden?
items.e: Length: 3 − (−4) = 7 m. Width: 1 − (−3) = 4 m. Perimeter = 7 + 4 + 7 + 4 = 22 m. (28 is the area in square metres; 11 goes only halfway around.)

items.q: A rectangle is 5 units wide and 3 units tall. Its bottom-left vertex is at (−1, −1). Where is its top-right vertex?
items.e: Go right 5 for the width: −1 + 5 = 4. Go up 3 for the height: −1 + 3 = 2. The vertex is (4, 2). (5, 3) forgets to start from (−1, −1).

sets.title: Graph a table of values: BC word problems

items.q: On a winter morning in Prince George, the temperature rises 2 °C each hour. Which ordered pair (x, y) shows the temperature at 8 a.m.?
items.e: 8 a.m. is 2 hours after 6 a.m., so x = 2. The table gives y = −1. Write x first: (2, −1). (x is hours after 6 a.m., not the clock time.)

items.q: This graph shows the Prince George temperatures (x = hours after 6 a.m., y = temperature in °C). The points for which hours are in Quadrant IV?
items.e: Quadrant IV needs x positive and y negative. Hours 1 and 2 have temperatures below 0 °C. Hour 0, (0, −5), is on the y-axis, so it is not in a quadrant.

items.q: In Prince George it is 3 °C at 10 a.m. (x = 4). The temperature keeps rising 2 °C each hour. What is the temperature at 11 a.m.?
items.e: 11 a.m. is x = 5, one hour after x = 4. Add 2 °C: 3 + 2 = 5 °C. The point is (5, 5). (4 °C adds only 1; 7 °C adds 2 hours.)

items.q: Owen owes his sister $6, so his balance is −$6. He pays back $2 each week. He graphs (week, balance) for weeks 0 to 3. Which point is plotted in the wrong place?
items.e: The pairs are (0, −6), (1, −4), (2, −2), (3, 0). Point B is at (−4, 1): x and y are swapped. It should be at (1, −4).

items.q: Owen’s balance starts at −$6 and goes up $2 each week. In which week does his graph reach the x-axis (balance $0)?
items.e: −$6 + $2 + $2 + $2 = $0, so it takes 3 weeks. The point is (3, 0), on the x-axis. (6 forgets that he pays $2 each week.)

items.q: Owen’s balance starts at −$6 (week 0) and goes up $2 each week. Which ordered pair (week, balance) shows his balance after week 1?
items.e: After 1 week: −6 + 2 = −4. x = 1 and y = −4: (1, −4). (−2 is week 2’s balance.)

items.q: Leah is scuba diving off Vancouver Island. She starts at the surface and goes down 2 m each minute. Which rule matches the table?
items.e: Each minute, y goes down by 2, and y = 0 when x = 0. So y = −2 × x. Check: x = 3 gives −2 × 3 = −6.

items.q: This graph shows Leah’s dive (x = minutes, y = depth in metres). In which quadrant are the points after the start?
items.e: After the start, x is positive (time goes on) and y is negative (below the surface). Right and down is Quadrant IV. The start, (0, 0), is the origin.

items.q: Ji-woo makes a table of values for y = x + 2. What is the missing value?
items.e: x = −1. y = −1 + 2 = 1. (3 forgets the minus sign; −3 subtracts 2.)

items.q: Ji-woo graphs the points from the table. Which rule matches the graph?
items.e: Read a point: (0, 2). With y = x + 2, x = 0 gives 2. Check (−3, −1): −3 + 2 = −1. y = 2x gives 0 at x = 0, so it does not match.

items.q: Ji-woo’s table for y = x + 2 has x = −3, −2, −1, 0 and 1. Which of its points is on the y-axis?
items.e: A point on the y-axis has x = 0. When x = 0, y = 0 + 2 = 2, so the point is (0, 2). ((−2, 0) is the table’s point on the x-axis.)

items.q: Simran is coding a game. Her sprite moves along these points: (−2, −5), (−1, −3), (0, −1) and (1, 1). Which point comes next in the pattern?
items.e: x goes up by 1 each time and y goes up by 2. After (1, 1) comes (1 + 1, 1 + 2) = (2, 3).

items.q: Simran changes her sprite’s path. This graph shows the new path. When x goes up by 1, how does y change?
items.e: From (−3, −3) to (−2, −1), x goes up 1 and y goes from −3 to −1, up 2. Each point is 1 right and 2 up from the one before.

items.q: At a dock in Nanaimo, the water level is measured from its average level. The tide goes out, so the level drops 1 m each hour. Which ordered pair shows when the water is at its average level (0 m)?
items.e: The level is 0 m at hour 3, so x = 3 and y = 0: (3, 0). (0, 3) is the start, when the water is 3 m above average.

items.q: This graph shows the tide table. Which statement is true?
c: The points go up from left to right
The points are all in Quadrant I
The points go down from left to right
The points make a horizontal line
items.e: As x goes up by 1, y goes down by 1, so each point is 1 right and 1 down from the one before. The last point, (4, −1), is in Quadrant IV.

items.q: The water level at the Nanaimo dock is 1 m below average after 4 hours. Which point shows this?
items.e: x = 4 hours and y = −1 m (below average is negative). The point is (4, −1): point D.

items.q: On a ski day in Whistler, the temperature falls 3 °C each hour after 6 p.m. Which ordered pair shows the temperature at 10 p.m.?
items.e: 10 p.m. is 4 hours after 6 p.m., so x = 4. The table gives y = −6. The ordered pair is (4, −6).

items.q: The Whistler temperature keeps falling 3 °C each hour. Graph the point for 11 p.m. (x = 5). What is its y-coordinate?
items.e: x = 4 has y = −6. One more hour: −6 − 3 = −9. (−7 only subtracts 1; 9 drops the minus sign.)

items.q: A table shows x = 1, 2, 3 and y = −2, −4, −6. Noah graphs the points (−2, 1), (−4, 2) and (−6, 3). What mistake did he make?
c: He used y as the first coordinate
items.e: The ordered pairs are (x, y): (1, −2), (2, −4) and (3, −6). Noah wrote y first.

items.q: From a table of night temperatures in Kamloops, Kai must plot (2, −3). He plots it in Quadrant I. What mistake did he make?
items.e: y = −3 means 3 down, so (2, −3) is right 2 and down 3: Quadrant IV. Ignoring the minus sign puts it at (2, 3) in Quadrant I.
